title: Staufen purification: challenges and opportunities. Protocols and troubleshooting✰
author: Shakoor, Tripepi
materials: This protocol does not require EDTA, and it was initially used to purify the proteins described here. Due to high degradation rate, we abandoned this method, therefore, we decided to use protein purification method 2, 3, 4. However, this method is made of the following steps:1.Cell cracking2.Centrifuge the lysate at 39.000 g for 40 min at 4 °C3.Insert the supernatant into AKTA FPLC through a 0,45 µm filter4.Run FPLC IMAC I in His A and His B buffer (Table 2) for flow through and elution, respectively. Elution buffer is gradually added until reaching 100 %, Fig. 2). Flowrate 1 ml/min in flow-through and 4 ml in elution.5.Overnight TEV cleavage of the fractions containing the protein and dialysis in freshly prepared 2 L TEV buffer (Table 2).6.If the sample volume is higher than the sample loop volume, concentrate the elution fractions by a 10 kDa protein concentrator. We used Vivaspin 20 concentrators (Sartorius, Germany).7.Run IMAC II in His A and His B buffer for flow through and elution, respectively (same as step 4). Elution buffer is gradually added until reaching 100 %, Fig. 2). Flowrate 1 ml/min in flow-through and 4 ml in elution.8.Dialysis in agitation of protein in freshly prepared unfiltered SP-Sepharose buffer A for at least 6 h.9.Run FPLC in SP-Sepharose column in EDTA free buffer A and buffer B. Elution buffer is gradually added until reaching 100 %, Fig. 2). Flowrate 1 ml/min in flow-through and 4 ml in elution.10.Concentrate the elution fractions to 1 ml that contain intact protein by a 10 kDa protein concentrator, we used Vivaspin 20 concentrators (Sartorius, Germany).11.Add 15 µL SuperaseIN (Thermofisher, USA) to the sample and run it on a pre-equilibrated gel filtration Superdex™ 200 pg column (Avantor, USA) (Table 2).12.GF fractions that contain protein characterized by lowest degradation can be used for further experiments

steps.title: Prepare all required buffers
steps.instruction: Make the following buffers using the indicated components and concentrations: His‑A buffer: 1 M NaCl, 50 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8, 30 mM imidazole, 10 % (w/v) glycerol, 3.8 mM β‑mercaptoethanol; His‑B buffer: 0.5 M NaCl, 50 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8, 600 mM imidazole, 10 % (w/v) glycerol, 3.8 mM β‑mercaptoethanol; TEV buffer: 0.5 M NaCl, 50 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8, 10 % (w/v) glycerol, 3.8 mM β‑mercaptoethanol; Buffer A (EDTA‑free): 0.1 M NaCl, 50 mM Tris pH 8, 3.8 mM β‑mercaptoethanol, 0.25 mM EDTA; Buffer B (EDTA‑free): 1 M NaCl, 50 mM Tris pH 8, 3.8 mM β‑mercaptoethanol, 0.25 mM EDTA; Buffer A* (for hStau1/hStau1ΔSSM): 0.3 M NaCl, 50 mM Tris pH 7, 3.8 mM β‑mercaptoethanol, 0.5 mM EDTA; Buffer B* (for hStau1/hStau1ΔSSM): 1 M NaCl, 50 mM Tris pH 7, 3.8 mM β‑mercaptoethanol, 0.5 mM EDTA; GF buffer (methods 1‑2): 150 mM NaCl, 50 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.0, 3.8 mM β‑mercaptoethanol, 0.25 mM EDTA; GF* buffer (methods 3‑4): 1500 mM NaCl, 50 mM Tris pH 8, 3.8 mM β‑mercaptoethanol; GF buffer 2 (method 3): 4300 mM NaCl, 50 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7, 3.8 mM β‑mercaptoethanol; FA buffer: 150 mM NaCl, 50 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.0, 3.8 mM β‑mercaptoethanol, 0.25 mM EDTA. Filter all buffers through 0.45 µm membrane before use.

steps.title: Thaw cell pellets slowly
steps.instruction: Place frozen cell pellets on ice and allow them to thaw gradually to preserve protein integrity.

steps.title: Disrupt cells by high‑pressure homogenization
steps.instruction: Pass the thawed cell suspension through an EmulsiFlex C3 (Avestin, UK) at approximately 1500 bar. If the device is unavailable, use an ultrasound cell‑cracking method as an alternative.

steps.title: Clarify lysate by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the disrupted lysate at 39 000 g for 45 min at 4 °C (method 1 specifies 40 min; use 45 min as the standard).

steps.title: Load supernatant onto IMAC column (IMAC I)
steps.instruction: Filter the clarified supernatant through a 0.45 µm filter and inject it into a Cytiva AKTA PrimePlus using a 50 mL sample loop (5 mL loop for subsequent gel‑filtration runs). Run IMAC I with His‑A buffer as flow‑through (1 mL/min) and gradually add His‑B buffer as elution (4 mL/min) until 100 % His‑B is reached; collect a total flow‑through volume of 100 mL. Monitor absorbance at 280 nm and run 12 % SDS‑PAGE on fractions to assess protein integrity.

steps.title: Dialyze IMAC I eluate and perform TEV cleavage
steps.instruction: Transfer fractions containing the target protein into a dialysis bag (appropriate molecular‑weight cut‑off). Dialyze against 2 L TEV buffer (or buffer A* for method 4) while adding 1 mg TEV protease per sample. Stir with a magnetic stirrer at room temperature (~22 °C) for overnight incubation (for method 4 perform the cleavage at 4 °C).

steps.title: Run second IMAC (IMAC II) to remove TEV and uncut protein
steps.instruction: Load the TEV‑cleaved dialysate onto a fresh IMAC column using the same His‑A (flow‑through) and His‑B (elution) buffers as in IMAC I. Use flow‑through rate of 1 mL/min and elution rate of 4 mL/min, adding His‑B gradually to 100 %. Collect flow‑through fractions (cleaved, tag‑free protein) and elution fractions (His‑tagged TEV protease and any uncut protein).

steps.title: Dialyze IMAC II flow‑through into ion‑exchange buffer
steps.instruction: Place the IMAC II flow‑through (cleaved protein) into a dialysis bag and dialyze against 2 L buffer A (or buffer A* for methods 3‑4) with magnetic stirring for at least 6 h (or overnight). This step removes residual TEV protease and adjusts the sample to the SP‑Sepharose buffer conditions.

steps.title: Perform cation exchange chromatography (SP)
steps.instruction: Load the dialyzed sample onto an SP‑Sepharose column equilibrated with buffer A (or buffer A*). Run the column at 1 mL/min for flow‑through, then apply a linear gradient of buffer B (or buffer B*) up to 100 % at 4 mL/min. Discard flow‑through (aggregated/RNA‑bound protein) and collect elution fractions containing RNA‑free protein. Use only SP‑eluted fractions for downstream steps.

steps.title: Concentrate SP‑eluted fractions
steps.instruction: Concentrate the pooled SP‑eluted fractions with a 10 kDa centrifugal concentrator (e.g., Vivaspin 20, Sartorius). Reduce the volume to ≤5 mL (method 1 reduced to 1 mL) before size‑exclusion chromatography.

steps.title: Size‑exclusion chromatography (gel filtration)
steps.instruction: Inject the concentrated sample into a Superdex™ 200 pg column (5 mL sample loop) using the appropriate gel‑filtration buffer: GF buffer for methods 1‑2, GF* buffer for methods 3‑4, or GF buffer 2 for method 3. Run at a constant flow rate of 1 mL/min. Collect fractions (typically 10–13 mL elution volume) and analyze by SDS‑PAGE; retain fractions showing the lowest degradation.

steps.title: Add RNase inhibitor and store
steps.instruction: To the pooled gel‑filtration fractions add 15 µL SuperaseIN (ThermoFisher, USA). Store the purified Staufen protein at the desired temperature for downstream experiments.
